   173	| Hands | On hips from start to landing | Discard the rep. Arm swing adds height and changes the strategy metrics |
   174	| Feet | Both feet on their own plate at takeoff and landing; no shuffle, no step off | Discard the rep. A foot that lands off a plate breaks the asymmetry numbers |
   175	| Effort | The two reps within [CONFIRM: allowed difference between reps] of each other | [CONFIRM: what to do when the two reps disagree, for example take a third rep] |
   176	| Landing | Stiff athletic landing, both feet, stuck without a step or a second bounce | A soft or absorbed landing does not change the takeoff metrics, but it changes the landing force metrics. Note it, and repeat the rep if landing metrics are being reported |
   177	| Count | Exactly 2 CMJ reps detected [CONFIRM: or 3 if a third rep is allowed] | If the app found an extra, check whether a reset bounce was read as a jump; delete it or re-run |
   178	| Profile | The right athlete | Wrong profile is the most expensive error. Fix it before saving, not in the database later |
   179	
   180	Reading the first numbers: jump height uses the impulse-momentum method
   181	(Jump Height, Imp-Mom), not flight time, because flight time is inflated by a tucked
   182	landing. RSI-modified is jump height divided by contraction time. Asymmetry is
   183	(left minus right) divided by the larger of the two, as a percentage. All three definitions
   184	are in the Operations Guide glossary. [CONFIRM: that Imp-Mom is the jump height variant in
   185	Baylor reports.]
   186	
   187	## Troubleshooting
   188	
   189	| Problem | Likely cause | What to do |
   190	|---|---|---|
   191	| Plates will not connect to the app | Cable loose, plates not powered, app on the wrong device | Reseat both cable ends, power cycle the plates, restart the app. [CONFIRM: whether Baylor's plates connect by USB or Bluetooth] |
   192	| Weigh-in never turns green | Athlete moving, plate rocking on uneven floor, something touching a plate | Still the athlete, move to a flatter spot, clear the plates and re-zero |
   193	| App finds the wrong number of reps | Reset bounce read as a jump, or the stabilize pause was too short | Delete the extra rep in review, or re-run with a longer still pause |
   194	| Left and right look swapped | Platform Assignment setting does not match the physical layout | Fix the setting before testing anyone else. Flag any sessions recorded with it wrong |
   195	| Numbers look off for one athlete | Wrong profile, wrong body weight, or arms came off hips | Check the profile and weight first. Review the video or ask the spotter |
   196	| Test will not save or export | Export folder missing or disconnected; cloud sync not signed in | Check the Auto Test Export Folder path and the VALD Hub login. Data stays on the device until sync succeeds; do not clear it |
   197	| App freezes | Memory, or too many profiles in one recording | Close and restart the app. Keep recordings to one squad |
   198	| Battery or power lost mid-session | [CONFIRM: whether plates are battery or mains powered] | Saved reps are kept. Re-run the athlete who was on the plates |
   199	
   200	Vendor support: VALD support through the Hub help menu [CONFIRM: Baylor's VALD account
   201	contact, and the vendor support hours]. Do not share athlete data in a support ticket;
   202	describe the problem and send screenshots with names removed.
   203	
   204	## Data management and export
   205	
   206	Where the data goes, in order:
   207	
   208	1. **ForceDecks app** on the testing device. The raw force traces and the computed metrics.
   209	2. **VALD Hub** (cloud). Syncs from the app when the device is online. This is where staff
   210	   view results and build reports. [CONFIRM: that sync is automatic on this device.]
   211	3. **Kitman Labs.** The athlete management system of record. ForceDecks data reaches
   212	   Kitman from VALD Hub by API, for all sports. No CSV step.
   213	4. **Department database.** The force plate decision system and the CMJ traffic light pull
   214	   from VALD by API, for all sports, into a local DuckDB database for the Wednesday read.
   215	   [CONFIRM: who runs the pull.]
   216	
   217	File naming for any manual export follows the SOP template:
   218	`YYYY-MM-DD_SportCode_TestType_AthleteID`, for example `2026-10-23_WVB_CMJ_1234`.
   219	Use the athlete ID, not the name, in file names. [CONFIRM: the ID source and the sport code
   220	list.]
   221	
   222	After every session:
   223	
   224	- Confirm the session appears in VALD Hub with the right date, sport tag and athlete count.
   225	- If a rep was discarded and re-run, the discarded rep should not be in Hub.
   226	- Note anything unusual (fatigue, shoes, a late arrival) in the session note, not in a text
   227	  message.
   228	
   229	Who may see what: CMJ results are performance data, not health data, under the draft
   230	NCAA guide's classification. They go to the athlete, the Athletic Performance coach, the sport
   231	coach through the agreed report, and Athletic Medicine when return-to-play is involved.
   232	Identifiable results never go into email to outside parties, personal cloud storage, code
   233	repositories or unapproved AI tools. The full rules are the guide's section 4 and the
   234	Digest's Part 3.
   235	
   236	Retention: [CONFIRM: how long raw traces are kept on the device and in Hub; the NCAA
   237	guide leaves the retention period pending General Counsel.]
   238	
   239	## Teardown and storage
   240	
   241	1. Stop recording and confirm the last save.
   242	2. Confirm sync to VALD Hub if the device is online; if not, sync as soon as it is.
   243	3. Power down the plates and the device.
   244	4. Disconnect cables; coil, do not bend at the connector.
   245	5. Wipe the plate surfaces.
   246	6. Return everything to the case in its labeled spot and the case to its storage location
   247	   [CONFIRM: location]. Put the device on charge.
   248	
   249	## Who to contact
   250	
   251	| Question | Contact |
   252	|---|---|
   253	| The protocol, cues, or whether to postpone a test | Director of Applied Performance |
   254	| Running the test day to day, equipment location | [CONFIRM: Associate Director of Applied Performance or the daily user named above] |
   255	| An athlete returning from injury | Athletic Medicine staff for that sport, then the Director |
   256	| App, plates, Hub login | Vendor support through VALD Hub; then the Director |
   257	| Data in the department database or the Wednesday read | [CONFIRM: owner of the force plate decision system] |
   258	
   259	Phone numbers and emails live in the Digest appendix contact table, not here, so a staff
   260	change does not orphan this chapter.
   261	
   262	## Revision history
   263	
   264	| Date | Author | Change | Version |
   265	|---|---|---|---|
   266	| 2026-10-04 | Drafted for Eric Rash | First draft from the V3 protocol, the Operations Guide ForceDecks section, the SOP template, and the Iowa manual's format | 0.1 |
   267	| 2026-10-06 | Eric Rash answers; invented defaults turned into placeholders | 2 reps (not 3), stiff athletic landing (not soft), ForceDecks app 2.1, VALD to Kitman and department database by API for all sports | 0.2 |
   268	
   269	## Open questions for Eric
   270	
   271	Answered 2026-10-06:
   272	
   273	- **Protocol:** live. 2 reps, hands on hips (V3 said 3; the staff run 2).
   274	- **App version:** ForceDecks 2.1, the latest. Check it once on the device.
   275	- **Landing:** stiff athletic landing. Landing force metrics are now comparable to
   276	  published stiff-landing data.
   277	- **Data path:** VALD Hub to Kitman Labs and to the department database by API, all sports.
   278	
   279	Still open before the 10/23 ship. Each one is also a [CONFIRM] tag above.
   280	
   281	1. **Who is the daily user and co-owner of this chapter?** The ship rule needs a named
   282	   person who will run it, mark it up, and answer the 30-day check on 11/22.
   283	2. **Which metrics are reported** for daily readiness and for coach reports, and is Jump
   284	   Height (Imp-Mom) the variant in use?
   285	3. **Equipment facts:** plate model and serials, testing device name, storage location,
   286	   vault name, sport code list, athlete ID source.
   287	4. **Does this chapter replace the ForceDecks section of the Operations Guide** once it
   288	   ships, or do both stand until the Digest covers all of Part 2?

===== B_cmj V3 protocol: testing conditions, warm-up, and Countermovement Jump 1180
##### A_fd
Prior to Testing
• Log in – Log in to ForceDecks Jump
• Confirm settings – Confirm the following settings:
o Layout > Operational Mode is set to “Shared”
o Layout > Show Profile Selection Pane is set to “Always”
o Platforms > Sequenced Platform Count is set to “1”
o Platforms > Platform Assignment is correct for your plate setup
o Platforms > Auto Test Export Folder is the same folder as ForceDecks
Starting a Test
• Confirm test queue – Double click profile names to add them to the testing queue.
• Start testing – Click “Play” button.
• Confirm weighing – Click “Weigh Start” or “Start” to confirm your weighing option.
• Zero sensors – Ensure nothing is touching the plates before allowing the plates to zero.
Recording a Test
• Assume starting position – Ask the first individual (profile) in the testing queue to assume the starting position on the plates.
• Perform rep – Instruct the individual to perform the required movement/jump.
• Repeat rep – Have the individual pause for 2-3 seconds, then repeat the movement/jump for the required number of reps.
• Select next individual (profile) – Select the next individual in the testing queue and repeat steps 1-4. Up to 16 profiles may be
tested before stopping the recording.
• Stop recording – Click “Stop” button to examine all results.
• Review – Review and edit results as required.
• Save – Click “Save” to select reps, apply tags and notes; or click “Save All” to save.
##### A_metrics1
Take-Off Phase Metrics
• Braking Phase Duration – time period of the Eccentric Braking Phase; in second(s)
• Braking Phase Duration:Concentric Duration – ratio of Braking Phase Duration to Concentric Phase Duration;
unitless
• Braking Phase Duration:Contraction Time – ratio of Braking Phase Duration to Contraction Time; unitless
• CMJ Stiffness – Peak Vertical Force during the Concentric Phase divided by the displacement at the start of the
Concentric Phase (i.e., minimum displacement); in Newtons per meter (N/m)
• Concentric Duration – time period of the Concentric Phase; in milliseconds (ms)
• Concentric Impulse – net impulse during the Concentric Phase; in Newton seconds (N s)
• Concentric Impulse (Abs) / BM – Absolute Impulse during the Concentric Phase divided by Body Mass; in Newton
seconds per kilogram (N s/kg)
• Concentric Impulse-100ms – Net Impulse during the first 100ms of the Concentric Phase; in Newton seconds (N s)
• Concentric Impulse-100ms:Concentric Impulse – ratio of Concentric Impulse 100ms to Concentric Impulse;
unitless
• Concentric Impulse-50ms – Net Impulse during the first 50ms of the Concentric Phase; in Newton seconds (N s)
• Concentric Maximum RFD – Peak RFD over a 50ms window during the Concentric Phase; in Newtons per second
(N/s)
• Concentric Mean Force / BM – Concentric Mean Force divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per kilogram (N/kg)
##### A_metrics2
• Concentric Mean Force – average Vertical Force during the Concentric Phase; in Newtons (N)
• Concentric Mean Power / BM – Concentric Mean Power divided by Body Mass; in Watts per kilogram (W/kg)
• Concentric Mean Power – Average Power during the Concentric Phase; in Watts (W)
• Concentric Mean Velocity – Average Velocity during the Concentric Phase; in Meters per second (m/s)
• Concentric Peak Force – Maximum Vertical Force during the Concentric Phase; in Newtons (N)
• Concentric Peak Force / BM – Concentric Peak Force divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per kilogram (N/kg)
• Concentric Peak Velocity – Maximum Velocity during the Concentric Phase; in Meters per second (m/s)
• Concentric RFD - RFD between the start of the Concentric Phase and Peak Concentric Force. 0 will be reported if
Total Vertical Force slopes downward; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Concentric RFD – 100ms – RFD during the first 100ms of the Concentric Phase; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Concentric RFD – 200ms – RFD during the first 200ms of the Concentric Phase; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Concentric RFD – 50ms – RFD during the first 50ms of the Concentric Phase; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Concentric RFD / BM – Concentric RFD divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per second per kilogram (N/s/kg)
##### A_metrics3
• Concentric RPD – RPD from the start of the Concentric Phase to the point when Peak Power occurs; in Watts per second
(W/s)
• Concentric RPD – 100ms – RPD during the first 100ms of the Concentric Phase; in Watts per second (W/s)
• Concentric RPD – 50ms – RPD during the first 50ms of the Concentric Phase; in Watts per second (W/s)
• Concentric RPD / BM – Concentric RPD divided by Body Mass; in Watts per second per kilogram (W/s/kg)
• Concentric RPD-100ms / BM – Concentric RPD 100ms divided by Body Mass; in Watts per second per kilogram (W/s/kg)
• Concentric RPD-50ms / BM – Concentric RPD 50ms divided by Body Mass; in Watts per second per kilogram (W/s/kg)
• Concentric Time to Peak Force – time period for the start of the Concentric Phase to the point when Peak Force occurs; in
milliseconds (ms)
• Contraction Time – time period from Start of Movement to Take-off; in milliseconds (ms)
• Contraction Time:Eccentric Duration – ratio of Contraction Time to Eccentric Duration; as a percentage (%)
• Countermovement Depth – Maximum Displacement between Start of Movement to Take-off; in centimeters (cm)
• Displacement at Take-off – Displacement from initial starting position to take-off (i.e., standing upright to leaving the force
plates); in centimeters (cm)
• Eccentric Acceleration Phase Duration – time period of the Eccentric Acceleration Phase (i.e., from Start of Movement to
##### A_metrics4
the point when maximum negative Velocity occurs); in seconds (s)
• Eccentric Braking Impulse – Net Impulse during the Eccentric Braking Phase; in Newton seconds (N s)
• Eccentric Braking RFD / BM – Eccentric Braking RFD divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per second per kilogram (N/s/kg)
• Eccentric Braking RFD – RFD over the full Eccentric Braking Phase; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Eccentric Braking RFD-100ms – RFD during the first 100ms of the Eccentric Braking Phase; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Eccentric Deceleration – Net Impulse during the Eccentric Deceleration Phase; in Newton seconds (N s)
• Eccentric Deceleration Impulse / BM – Eccentric Deceleration Impulse divided by Body Mass; in Newton seconds per
kilogram (N s/kg)
• Eccentric Deceleration Phase Duration – time period of the Eccentric Deceleration Phase; in seconds (s)
• Eccentric Deceleration RFD – RFD over the full Eccentric Deceleration Phase; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Eccentric Deceleration RFD / BM – Eccentric Deceleration RFD divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per second per kilogram
(N/s/kg)
• Eccentric Duration – time period of the Eccentric Phase; in milliseconds (ms)
• Eccentric Mean Braking Force – Average Vertical Force during the Eccentric Braking Phase; in Newtons (N)
• Eccentric Mean Deceleration Force – Average Vertical Force during the Eccentric Deceleration Phase; in Newtons (N)
##### A_metrics5
• Eccentric Mean Force – Average Vertical Force during the Eccentric Phase, equivalent to Body Weight (N); in Newtons (N)
• Eccentric Mean Power – Average Power during the Eccentric Phase; in Watts (W)
• Eccentric Mean Power / BM – Eccentric Mean Power divided by Body Mass; in Watts per kilogram (W/kg)
• Eccentric Peak Force – Maximum Vertical Force during the Eccentric Phase; in Newtons (N)
• Eccentric Peak Force / BM – Eccentric Peak Force divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per kilogram (N/kg)
• Eccentric Peak Power – Maximum Power during the Eccentric Phase; in Watts (W)
• Eccentric Peak Power:Concentric Peak Power – ratio of Eccentric Peak Power to Concentric Peak Power; unitless
• Eccentric Peak Velocity – Macimum Velocity during the Eccentric Phase; in milliseconds (ms)
• Eccentric Unloading Impulse – Net Impulse during the Eccentric Unloading Phase (i.e., from Start of Movement to the start of
the Eccentric Deceleration Phase); in Newton seconds (N s)
• Eccentric Concentric Duration – ratio of Eccentric Duration to Concentric Duration; as a percentage (%)
• Eccentric Concentric Mean Force Ratio – ratio of Eccentric Mean Force to Concentric Mean Force; as a percentage (%)
• Flight Time – time period between Take-off and Landing; in milliseconds (ms)
• Flight Time:Contraction Time – ratio of Flight Time to Contraction Time; unitless
##### A_metrics6
• Flight Time:Eccentric Duration – ratio of Flight Time to Eccentric Duration; unitless
• Force at Peak Power – Vertical Force at the point when Peak Power occurs; in Newtons (N)
• Force at Zero Velocity – Vertical Force at the point when zero Velocity occurs prior to Take-off; in Newtons (N)
• Force at Zero Velocity / BM – Force at Zero Velocity divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per kilogram (N/kg)
• Jump Height (Flight Time) – Jump Height calculated from Flight Time; in centimeters (cm)
• Jump Height (Flight Time) in Inches – Jump Height (Flight Time) converted to inches; in inches (in)
• Jump Height (FT) Relative Landing RFD – Landing RFD divided by Jump Height (Flight Time); in Newtons per second per
centimeter (N/s/cm)
• Jump Height (FT) Relative Peak Landing Force – Peak Landing Force divided by Jump Height (Flight Time); in Newtons per
centimeter (N/cm)
• Lower-Limb Stiffness – Change in Vertical Force during the Eccentric Phase divided by Countermovement Depth; in Newtons
per meter (N/m)
• Mean Eccentric+Concentric Power:Time – Mean Power between Start of Movement and Take-off, divided by Contraction
Time; in Watts per second (W/s)
• Minimum Eccentric Force – Minimum Vertical Force during the Eccentric Phase; in Newtons (N)
• Movement Start to Peak Force – Time Period between Start of Movement and the point when Peak Vertical Force occurs
##### A_metrics7
prior to Take-off; in seconds (s)
• Movement Start to Peak Power – Time Period between Start of Movement and the point when Peak Power occurs prior to
Take-off; in seconds (s)
• P1 Concentric Impulse – Net Impulse during the first 50% of the Concentric Phase (time-wise); in Newton seconds (N s)
• P2 Concentric Impulse – Net Impulse during the second 50% of the Concentric Phase (time-wise); in Newton seconds (N s)
• P2 Concentric Impulse:P1 Concentric Impulse – Ratio of P2 Concentric Impulse to P1 Concentric Impulse; unitless
• Peak Net Take-off Force / BM – Maximum Vertical Force between Start of Movement and Take-off, - Body Weight, and divided
by Body Mass; in Newtons per kilogram (N/kg)
• Peak Power – Maximum Power during the Concentric Phase; in Watts (W)
• Peak Power / BM – Peak Power divided by Body Mass; in Watts per kilogram (W/kg)
• Peak Take-off Acceleration – Maximum Acceleration of the Center of Mass between Start of Movement and Take-off; in
Meters per second squared (m/s2)
• Positive Impulse – Net Impulse during the entire repetition (eccentric, concentric, and landing combined); in Newton seconds
(N s)
• Positive Take-off Impulse – Net Impulse during Take-off (eccentric and concentric phases combined); in Newton seconds (N
s)
• RSI-modified – Jump Height (Flight Time) divided by Contraction Time; in meters per second (m/s)
##### A_metrics8
• RSI-modified (Imp-Mom) – Jump Height (Imp-Mom) divided by Contraction Time; in meters per second (m/s)
Landing Phase Metrics
• Jump Height (Imp-Dis) – Maximum Displacement of the Center of Mass between Take-off and Landing; in centimeters (cm)
• Jump Height (Imp-Mom) – Jump Height calculated from the Velocity of the Center of Mass at the instant of Take-off and Body
Mass; in centimeters (cm)
• Jump Height (Imp-Mom) in Inches – Jump Height (Imp-Mom) converted to inches; in inches (in)
• Landing Impulse – Absolute Impulse from Landing to the point when Peak Landing Force occur; in Newton seconds (N s)
• Landing Net Peak Force / BM – Maximum Vertical Force after Landing, - Body Weight, and divided by Body Mass; in Newtons
per kilogram (N/kg)
• Landing RFD – RFD between Landing and the point when Peak Landing Force occurs; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Landing RFD 50ms – RFD of the first 50ms following Landing; in Newtons per second (N/s)
• Mean Landing Power – Average Power between Landing and the end of the rep; in Watts (W)
• Peak Landing Acceleration – Maximum Acceleration of the Center of Mass between Landing and the end of the rep; in meters
per second squared (m/s2)
• Peak Landing Force – Maximum Vertical Force after Landing; in Newtons (N)
• Peak Landing Force / BM – Peak Landing Force divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per kilogram (N/kg)
##### A_metrics9
• Peak Landing Power – Maximum Power between Landing and the end of the rep; in Watts (W)
• Peak Landing Velocity – Maximum Velocity of the Center of Mass between Landing and the end of the rep; in meters per
second (m/s)
• Take-off Peak Force – Maximum Vertical Force between Start of Movement and Take-off; in Newtons (N)
• Take-off Peak Force / BM – Take-off Peak Force divided by Body Mass; in Newtons per kilogram (N/kg)
• Time to Braking Phase – time period between Start of Movement and the beginning of the Eccentric Braking Phase; in
seconds (s)
• Total Work – Integration of Power (i.e., area under the Power-Time curve) between Start of Movement and Take-off; in Joules
(J)
• Velocity at Peak Power – Velocity of the Center of Mass at the point when Peak Power between Start of Movement and Take-
off occurs; in meters per second (m/s)
• Vertical Velocity at Take-off – Velocity of the Center of Mass at the point when Take-off occurs; in meters per second (m/s)
For more information on jump metrics, visit the VALD ForceDecks Technical Glossary.
To access the ForceDecks user guide, click HERE.
##### B
BAYLOR UNIVERSITY
APPLIED PERFORMANCE
Testing Protocol
Testing can be performed under the following conditions.
Condition 1: Performing tests within a training session
Warm up: Team training warm up
Condition 2: Performing tests outside of a training session
Standard Warm up:
Line hops (Forward/Backward/Left/Right) x 10 each
Open gate/Close gate (Hip internal/external rotation) x 5 each
Rapid Squat to Stand (Triple Extension) x 5 each

Countermovement Jump
Starting position:
Normal standing posture.
Hands on hips (if unweighted) or hands on barbell (if weighted).
Chest up and looking forward.
ForceDecks protocol:
Assume starting position – Ask the individual to assume starting position on the plates.
Weigh individual – Click “Weigh Athlete”. The individual must remain completely still, and the color display must register green before accepting body weight
Start recording – Click “Start Recording”.
Perform jump – Instruct the individual to:
Keep the chest up and looking forward.
Bend down.
Jump up.
Land softly.
Assume starting position again.
Repeat jump total of 3 countermovement jumps.
Stop recording – Click “Stop Recording”.
Analyze – Click “Analyze and Save”.

content.content:
##### A_tech1
TECHNOLOGY OVERVIEW
Catapult GPS tracking devices measure various forms of athletic workload in field-based
sports (e.g., high-velocity sprint exposures, heart rate, distance covered, and total
number of accelerations and decelerations).
Catapult OpenField Online platform used to access GPS performance analytics and create data
visualizations.
Kitman Labs Athlete management system (AMS) that acts as a central data storage site for
multiple technologies. Allows for scalable data analysis and visualization across
Baylor sport teams.
Perch Camera-based system that utilizes both hardware and software for Velocity Based
Training (VBT) and weight room performance monitoring.
Polar Chest strap heart rate sensor that measures electrical activity of the heart.
Utilized for aerobic performance and recovery, as well as a gauge for activity
intensity.
VALD DynaMo Handheld dynamometer and inclinometer used to assess strength and range of
motion.
VALD ForceDecks Dual, uniaxial force plates that analyze jumps, strength, power, asymmetry, and
more.
VALD ForceFrame Isometric testing device to quantify and train muscle strength in the upper and
lower extremities (e.g., knee flexion, shoulder internal/external rotation) and
measure limb asymmetry.
VALD Hub Online platform that promotes the generation and sharing of reports with
performance team members.
##### A_tech2
VALD NordBord Hamstring testing device used to quantify and train hamstring strength and
measure limb asymmetry.
VALD SmartSpeed Timing gate system used to measure speed, agility, and reactivity.
##### A_defs1
Technical Definitions
• Absolute – the magnitude of a given value (irrespective of being positive or negative)
• Acceleration – rate of change in velocity over time of the centre of mass (m/s2)
• Asymmetry – a relative measurement of difference between two sided values expressed as a percentage.
Calculated as (Left Metric value – Right Metric value) / maximum of (Left Metric value or Right Metric value) x 100
• Body Mass (BM) – measure of mass collected during weighing (kg)
• Body Weight (BW) – mass captured during the ‘Weigh Profile’ stage (N)
• Center of Mass (CoM) – the balance point of the body that mass is distributed about
• Displacement/Height – change in the vertical position of the Centre of Mass
• Force – strength as an attribute of physical action or movement
• Impulse (Absolute Impulse) – integration (area under the curve) of Force over a given period time period (Ns)
• Impulse (Net Impulse) – area under the force curve over a given time period but only above body weight (Ns)
• Impulse (Positive Impulse) – area under the curve from the start of movement to take off (i.e.: eccentric and
concentric phases combined) but only above body weight (Ns)
• Left Force – the vertical Force component measured from the left force plate (N)
• Left Metric – metric calculated using only the Left Force
• Maximum/Peak – the highest or largest value within a dataset or phase
##### A_defs2
• Mean – average of all data points within a dataset or phase, including the start and end of the phase
• Minimum – the single lowest value within a dataset or phase
• Power – the work rate a force exerts on an object, calculated as force x velocity (W)
• Recording – an entire force-time dataset from the time Start Recording is clicked until Stop Recording is clicked
• Rep – short for repetition, a period of time in a recording during which a single instance of a test is performed
• Rate of Force Development (RFD) - Change in force over a given time period or phase (N/s)
• Right Force – the vertical Force component measured from the right force plate (N)
• Right Metric – metric calculated using only the Right Force
• Rate of Power Development (RPD) – change in power over a given time period or phase (W/s)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the chapter 1 consistency check: numbers in code, prose by Jev. Resumable.

    python digest_check/check.py --dry        # print one request, no API call
    python digest_check/check.py              # finished pairs in runs/jev.jsonl are skipped

Needs private/sections.json (sources.py) and private/claims.json (claims.py).

For every chapter claim and each source (A = Operations Guide, B = V3 protocol), plus
each plant against its target source only:
  1. Passage choice, in code. B is always the V3 preamble plus its CMJ section (see
     sources.py for why). A is the ForceDecks workflow (the Operations Guide's whole
     ForceDecks procedure) plus the one other A section with the highest IDF-weighted
     overlap with the claim's words, if any overlap; under 3,000 characters together.
     Picking one section alone let the big glossary chunks win on vocabulary size.
  2. Numbers, in code (numcheck.py), against the whole kept text of that source.
     Written to runs/numbers.jsonl: ids, keys and values, no source text.
  3. One Jev request with two Nouls. Digits and number words two..twenty are masked
     to [n] in both claim and passage, so Jev cannot judge a number even by accident.
     Raw probabilities go to runs/jev.jsonl: ids and probabilities only.
A pair is flagged when contradiction >= 0.50 and coverage >= 0.50 (report.py).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import re
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "zotero_classify"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
import jev_client  # noqa: E402  - the one reviewed HTTP path in this repo
import numcheck  # noqa: E402

PRIVATE = HERE / "private"
RUNS = HERE / "runs"
DEFAULT_A = "A_fd"

STOP = set("""a an the and or of to in on for with by at from as is are be it its this that these
those then than not no if into out up do does each any all your you they them their there when
while before after only per which what who how can may must should will so but also same one
""".split())

QUESTIONS = {
    "contradiction": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": (
            "Use only `source_passage` and `chapter_claim` in the state. Do not use outside "
            "knowledge of ForceDecks, VALD, force plates or testing practice. Numbers are "
            "masked as [n] and are checked elsewhere; ignore them. Question: does "
            "`source_passage` give a different instruction, cue, order of steps, button, "
            "condition, setting or definition for the same step or the same thing that "
            "`chapter_claim` describes? If the passage does not mention that step, answer no."),
        "criteria": {
            "true": "The passage covers the same step or item and tells the tester to do "
                    "it differently, in a different order, with a different button or "
                    "setting, or defines it differently.",
            "false": "The passage agrees with the claim, adds detail without conflict, "
                     "covers a different step or test, or does not mention this step.",
        },
    },
    "coverage": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": (
            "Use only `source_passage` and `chapter_claim` in the state. Do not use outside "
            "knowledge. Question: does `source_passage` address the same step, setting, "
            "definition or topic that `chapter_claim` describes at all, whether it agrees "
            "or not?"),
        "criteria": {
            "true": "The passage says something about the same step, setting, definition "
                    "or topic.",
            "false": "The passage is silent on it.",
        },
    },
}


def words(text: str) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    for w in re.findall(r"[a-z][a-z-]+", text.lower()):
        if w in STOP or len(w) < 3:
            continue
        out.append(w[:-1] if w.endswith("s") and len(w) > 4 else w)
    return out


class Chooser:
    """IDF-weighted overlap between a claim and each section of source A."""

    def __init__(self, sections: list[dict]):
        self.sections = sections
        self.sets = [set(words(s["title"] + " " + s["text"])) for s in sections]
        n = len(sections)
        df: dict[str, int] = {}
        for s in self.sets:
            for w in s:
                df[w] = df.get(w, 0) + 1
        self.idf = {w: math.log(1 + n / c) for w, c in df.items()}

    def pick(self, claim: str) -> dict:
        """The workflow section, plus the best-matching other section if any overlaps."""
        terms = set(words(claim))
        base = next(s for s in self.sections if s["id"] == DEFAULT_A)
        best, best_score = None, 0.0
        for sec, vocab in zip(self.sections, self.sets):
            if sec["id"] == DEFAULT_A:
                continue
            score = sum(self.idf.get(w, 0) for w in terms & vocab)
            if score > best_score + 1e-9:
                best, best_score = sec, score
        if best is None:
            return base
        text = f"[{base['title']}]\n{base['text']}\n\n[{best['title']}]\n{best['text']}"
        assert len(text) <= 3000, (best["id"], len(text))
        return {"id": f"{DEFAULT_A}+{best['id']}", "title": f"{base['title']} + {best['title']}",
                "text": text}


def load():
    sections = json.loads((PRIVATE / "sections.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    claims = json.loads((PRIVATE / "claims.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["claims"]
    with (HERE / "plants.csv").open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        plants = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    return sections, claims, plants


def build_pairs(sections, claims, plants) -> list[dict]:
    chooser = Chooser(sections["A"])
    b = sections["B"][0]
    pairs = []
    for c in claims:
        for src in ("A", "B"):
            sec = chooser.pick(c["text"]) if src == "A" else b
            pairs.append({"pair": f"{c['id']}|{src}", "claim_id": c["id"], "plant": False,
                          "source": src, "section_id": sec["id"], "section_title": sec["title"],
                          "text": c["text"], "claim_section": c["section"],
                          "passage": sec["text"]})
    by_id = {c["id"]: c for c in claims}
    for p in plants:
        src = p["target_source"]
        sec = chooser.pick(p["altered_text"]) if src == "A" else b
        pairs.append({"pair": f"{p['id']}|{src}", "claim_id": p["id"], "plant": True,
                      "source": src, "section_id": sec["id"], "section_title": sec["title"],
                      "text": p["altered_text"],
                      "claim_section": by_id[p["base_claim_id"]]["section"],
                      "passage": sec["text"]})
    return pairs


def state_for(pair: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "chapter_claim": numcheck.mask(pair["text"]),
        "chapter_section": pair["claim_section"],
        "source_name": pair["section_title"],
        "source_passage": numcheck.mask(pair["passage"]),
    }


def ask(pair: dict, key: str) -> dict:
    started = time.monotonic()
    delay = 2.0
    for attempt in range(4):
        try:
            answers = jev_client.system_one(state_for(pair), QUESTIONS, key, timeout=30.0)
            break
        except jev_client.JevError as e:
            transient = any(t in str(e) for t in ("429", "529", "timeout", "URLError"))
            if not transient or attempt == 3:
                raise
            time.sleep(delay)
            delay *= 2
    out = {}
    for name in QUESTIONS:
        a = answers.get(name)
        if not isinstance(a, dict) or not isinstance(a.get("noul"), (int, float)):
            raise jev_client.JevError(f"bad {name} answer: {a!r}")
        out[name] = round(float(a["noul"]), 4)
    return {"pair": pair["pair"], "claim_id": pair["claim_id"], "source": pair["source"],
            "section_id": pair["section_id"], "plant": pair["plant"], **out,
            "attempts": attempt + 1, "ms": int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)}


def write_numbers(sections, pairs) -> None:
    full = {k: "\n".join(s["text"] for s in v) for k, v in sections.items()}
    RUNS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with (RUNS / "numbers.jsonl").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for p in pairs:
            for row in numcheck.compare(p["text"], full[p["source"]], p["source"]):
                fh.write(json.dumps({"pair": p["pair"], "claim_id": p["claim_id"],
                                     "source": p["source"], "plant": p["plant"], **row}) + "\n")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dry", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    sections, claims, plants = load()
    pairs = build_pairs(sections, claims, plants)
    write_numbers(sections, pairs)
    if args.dry:
        print(json.dumps({"state": state_for(pairs[0]), "questions": QUESTIONS}, indent=1)[:3000])
        from collections import Counter
        print(Counter(p["section_id"] for p in pairs if p["source"] == "A"))
        return 0

    out = RUNS / "jev.jsonl"
    done = set()
    if out.exists():
        for line in out.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            try:
                done.add(json.loads(line)["pair"])
            except (ValueError, KeyError):
                continue
    todo = [p for p in pairs if p["pair"] not in done]
    print(f"{len(pairs)} pairs ({len(claims)} claims x 2 sources + {len(plants)} plants), "
          f"{len(done)} done, {len(todo)} to do")
    key = jev_client.api_key()
    failures = []
    started = time.monotonic()
    with out.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
        def work(p):
            try:
                return p, ask(p, key), None
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                return p, None, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        for p, res, err in pool.map(work, todo):
            if err:
                failures.append((p["pair"], err))
                continue
            fh.write(json.dumps(res) + "\n")
            fh.flush()
    print(f"wall {time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s, failures: {len(failures)}")
    for f in failures[:10]:
        print(" ", *f)
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

TECHNOLOGY WORKFLOWS

Step 1: Pre-Activity
Charging Equipment
• Units and Dock(s)
o Connect devices into dock ports
o Connect dock to power supply
o Once charging, devices should display a red light on top
o Devices are fully charged once red light turns green
• Receiver(s)
o C-Type cable inserts at bottom of receiver
o USB end can be attached into wall attachment
o Light on side of receiver will turn red indicating it is charging

Prior to Testing
•
•

Log in – Log in to ForceDecks Jump
Confirm settings – Confirm the following settings:
o Layout > Operational Mode is set to “Shared”
o Layout > Show Profile Selection Pane is set to “Always”
o Platforms > Sequenced Platform Count is set to “1”
o Platforms > Platform Assignment is correct for your plate setup
o Platforms > Auto Test Export Folder is the same folder as ForceDecks

Starting a Test
•
•
•
•

Confirm test queue – Double click profile names to add them to the testing queue.
Start testing – Click “Play” button.
Confirm weighing – Click “Weigh Start” or “Start” to confirm your weighing option.
Zero sensors – Ensure nothing is touching the plates before allowing the plates to zero.

Recording a Test
•
•
•
•
•
•

Assume starting position – Ask the first individual (profile) in the testing queue to assume the starting position on the plates.
Perform rep – Instruct the individual to perform the required movement/jump.
Repeat rep – Have the individual pause for 2-3 seconds, then repeat the movement/jump for the required number of reps.
Select next individual (profile) – Select the next individual in the testing queue and repeat steps 1-4. Up to 16 profiles may be
tested before stopping the recording.
Stop recording – Click “Stop” button to examine all results.
Review – Review and edit results as required.

•

Save – Click “Save” to select reps, apply tags and notes; or click “Save All” to save.

For a complete list of ForceDecks testing protocols, click HERE.

Absolute – the magnitude of a given value (irrespective of being positive or negative)
Acceleration – rate of change in velocity over time of the centre of mass (m/s2)
Asymmetry – a relative measurement of difference between two sided values expressed as a percentage.
Calculated as (Left Metric value – Right Metric value) / maximum of (Left Metric value or Right Metric value) x 100
Body Mass (BM) – measure of mass collected during weighing (kg)
Body Weight (BW) – mass captured during the ‘Weigh Profile’ stage (N)
Center of Mass (CoM) – the balance point of the body that mass is distributed about
Displacement/Height – change in the vertical position of the Centre of Mass
Force – strength as an attribute of physical action or movement
Impulse (Absolute Impulse) – integration (area under the curve) of Force over a given period time period (Ns)
Impulse (Net Impulse) – area under the force curve over a given time period but only above body weight (Ns)
Impulse (Positive Impulse) – area under the curve from the start of movement to take off (i.e.: eccentric and
concentric phases combined) but only above body weight (Ns)
Left Force – the vertical Force component measured from the left force plate (N)
Left Metric – metric calculated using only the Left Force
Maximum/Peak – the highest or largest value within a dataset or phase
Mean – average of all data points within a dataset or phase, including the start and end of the phase
Minimum – the single lowest value within a dataset or phase
Power – the work rate a force exerts on an object, calculated as force x velocity (W)
Recording – an entire force-time dataset from the time Start Recording is clicked until Stop Recording is clicked
Rep – short for repetition, a period of time in a recording during which a single instance of a test is performed
Rate of Force Development (RFD) - Change in force over a given time period or phase (N/s)
Right Force – the vertical Force component measured from the right force plate (N)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Numbers in the chapter, checked in code. Jev never sees or judges a number.

    python digest_check/numcheck.py --selftest     # no API, no source files needed

A numeric fact is (key, value). Keys come from two places:
  * a count followed within two words by a unit: "2 countermovement jumps" -> (jumps, 2),
    "2 to 3 second still pause" -> (seconds, 2-3), "Up to 16 profiles" -> (profiles, 16);
  * named settings and drills: "Sequenced Platform Count: 1", "version 2.1",
    "Line hops ... 10 each".

returns typed judgments and probabilities instead of generated text. The API key is
NOT stored in this repo; see Secrets below for where it lives on each machine.

the key resolves and the API answers.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.

  `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` are tracked in the `dotclaude` repo and pushed nightly.

refuted_flags.claim: c14 vs V3 (Jev 0.69) listed as a flag ('The Operations Guide describes buttons called Weigh Start and Play; the V3 protocol describes Weigh Athlete, Start Recording and Analyze and Save')
refuted_flags.why: The claim accurately describes both sources. V3 uses Weigh Athlete, Start Recording and Analyze and Save. The guide's workflow uses 'Play' and 'Weigh Start'. So this is a Jev false positive, not a contradiction. The builder had already called it a false positive, but it still sat in the flag list. Moved to 'Removed on review'.

refuted_flags.claim: c27, c28 and c30 flagged as numbers 'against the 2026-10-06 drafting rule (do not invent specifics)'
refuted_flags.why: These numbers are not invented. Performance_Playbook origin/digest-start docs/digest/sources.md section 7 and gap-update.md line 67 trace them to the Iowa manual: 'no food or caffeine 2 hours before, no severe fatigue 48 to 72 hours before' and '3 to 4 familiarization trials'. The chapter's revision history lists the Iowa manual as a drafting source. Reworded into a confirm-adoption item, which notes that the chapter narrows Iowa's 48 to 72 h to 48 h.

missed_contradictions.claim: c54 with c53 and c56 (Data quality, 'Reading the first numbers'). Jump height is Imp-Mom, 'not flight time'; 'RSI-modified is jump height divided by contraction time'; 'All three definitions are in the Operations Guide glossary.'
missed_contradictions.source_says: Operations Guide glossary (A): 'RSI-modified – Jump Height (Flight Time) divided by Contraction Time' and, as a separate entry, 'RSI-modified (Imp-Mom) – Jump Height (Imp-Mom) divided by Contraction Time'. The metric named plain RSI-modified is the flight-time version the chapter rejects. Jev scored c54 vs A at 0.03 because c54 was sent alone with the flight-time chunk (A_metrics7).

missed_contradictions.claim: c17 (Zero the plates): 'Click Play (or Start). Make sure nothing is touching the plates, then let them zero.'
missed_contradictions.source_says: Operations Guide (A): 'Start testing – Click "Play" button.' then 'Confirm weighing – Click "Weigh Start" or "Start" to confirm your weighing option.' then 'Zero sensors'. In the guide, Start is the weighing-confirm button, not another name for Play. The chapter folds it into Play and drops the weighing-option step. Low severity; it belongs under the 2.1-screens [CONFIRM]. Jev scored it 0.25.

missed_contradictions.claim: c63 (Troubleshooting, App freezes): 'too many profiles in one recording ... Keep recordings to one squad'
missed_contradictions.source_says: This follows the guide's queue model ('Up to 16 profiles may be tested before stopping the recording') and conflicts with the chapter's own per-athlete loop and with V3's single-individual flow. It is the same issue as the c16 hand finding, which did not list it. Added to that item.
